newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market not established-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market not established-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet and not established after midday, feedlot sources said.
Bids were scattered at $69.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week's sales. Owners were pricing cattle at $72.00.

Feedlot cattle prices this week were expected to be supported by reduced showlists, compared with last week, and continued tight supplies of finished cattle on those lists, market sources said. The showlist in the Panhandle was estimated near 64,000 head, down 6,500 from last week and Kansas' showlist was pegged near 53,000, down 2,700.
Light support in feedlot cattle prices also was likely if beef demand heats up, the market sources said.
Retailers were expected to feature beef for a period squeezed between the end of October National Pork Month promotions and before holiday turkey and ham features start.
Beef should retain a good feature lead the first two weekends going into Thanksgiving Day, the sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.10 to up $0.10 per cwt, with 22 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
